The first component, institutional development and legal reform objective is to strengthen Sierra Leone's legal and institutional framework for land administration by supporting analyses and reform of the relevant legal framework, buildings, operational support, institutional strategies, capacity building, and sensitization campaigns. It consists of following sub-components: (i) institutional development; (ii) legal reform; and (iii) sensitization. The second component, land information system development will finance the procurement of required information and communication technology (ICT) equipment and establishing appropriate ICT infrastructure, business processes re-engineering, design, and development of a modern land information system (LIS) for automation of land administration processes, digitization of paper archives, containing deeds and cadastral maps, development of ICT and digital archive strategies, conducting cyber-security audit, and providing base maps and a geodetic network. It consists of following sub-components: (i) establishment of a land information system; (ii) base mapping and land cadastre; and (iii) geodetic network. The third component, recording and registration of land tenure rights is to improve records of land tenure rights and the processes how these rights can be transferred whether by inheritance, sale, or lease, or for some other third-party rights. The fourth component, project management will finance all expenses required to ensure efficient and transparent project management and coordination. The fifth component, contingent emergency response component (CERC) will draw from the uncommitted grant resources under the project from other project components to cover emergency response.

title: Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project
description: Supports Sierra Leone's digital transformation through broadband infrastructure, digital government systems, digital financial services, and digital skills development.

title: Digital Connectivity in Schools to Accelerate COVID-19 Education Response — Sierra Leone (Giga Phase 2)
description: Joint project between UNICEF Sierra Leone and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) to connect 523 schools to the internet. The IsDB approved a USD 5 million loan in September 2021 (Sierra Leone Parliament ratified October 2022). Under the co-financing arrangement, IsDB covers connectivity for 403 schools and UNICEF covers 120 schools. Building on the Giga Phase 1 pilot that connected 42 schools. Project aims to scale to 11,000 schools ultimately. Sierra Leone connected 39 hard-to-reach schools by 2023 (Giga Annual Results 2023). Internet costs reduced from USD 12,000 to USD 1,500 per school per year (87.5% reduction). Part of Giga's global initiative (UNICEF-ITU).

title: Escotel Sierra Leone – Solar Power for Telecom Towers Guarantee
description: MIGA political risk guarantee of $13.5 million to Escotel Mauritius covering its investment in Escotel (SL) Limited, which installs and operates solar-hybrid power systems at telecom tower sites (TNS) in Sierra Leone. Escotel installs solar PV panels replacing diesel generators at ~600 telecom network sites owned/operated by Orange Sierra Leone. Reduces diesel fuel use by 75% and avoids 58,000 tCO2e over the guarantee period. Risks: Transfer Restriction, Expropriation, War and Civil Disturbance for up to 10 years.

title: China Eximbank provides RMB 207 million government concessional loan for Phase 2 of National Fibre Optic Backbone Infrastructure Project (Linked to Project ID#30254)
description: On June 23, 2019, the Chinese Government and the Government of Sierra Leone signed a preferential loan framework agreement for Phase 2 of the National Fibre Optic Backbone Infrastructure Project. Then, on August 26, 2019, China Eximbank and the the Government of Sierra Leone’s Ministry of Finance signed an RMB 207,000,000 government concessional loan (GCL) agreement [CHINA EXIMBANK GCL NO (2019) 10 TOTAL No. (681)] for Phase 2 of the National Fibre Optic Backbone Infrastructure Project. The GCL agreement was then ratified by Sierra Leone’s Parliament on September 19, 2019. The borrowing terms of the GCL are as follows: a 20-year maturity, a 5-year grace period, a 1% interest rate, a 0.25% (RMB 517,500) management fee, and a 0.25% commitment fee. The borrower is responsible for repaying the loan between 2024 and 2039. Under the terms of the agreement, Government of Sierra Leone’s Ministry of Finance is also responsible for on-lending the proceeds of the GCL to a state-owned enterprise in Sierra Leone known as Sierra Leone Cable Company Limited (SALCAB). SALCAB, in turn, is expected to use the proceeds of the GCL to finance a $30 million commercial contract (ID#0002881900010V) between the Government of Sierra Leone’s Ministry of Information and Communications and Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd., which was signed on April 11, 2019. SALCAB signed an on-lending agreement with the Ministry of Finance on August 22, 2019.   The purpose of the project is to lay a 721.5-kilometer fiber-optic network that covers 15 major cities in the northern, eastern and southern regions of Sierra Leone.  Upon completion, the telecommunications infrastructure is expected to allow telecommunications operators to offer 3G and 4G services.   Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. is the EPC contractor responsible for implementation. title: SONATEL Mobile Telecom Services – Orange Sierra Leone Guarantee
description: MIGA issued guarantees of $97.2 million to Senegalese telecommunications company SONATEL S.A. covering its 50% equity stake in mobile operator Orange Sierra Leone Ltd (OSL). The acquisition facilitates modernization and expansion of OSL's network in Sierra Leone through deployment of additional telecom towers, improvement in network services, quality and reliability. Supported by IDA18 Private Sector Window (PSW) MIGA Guarantee Facility. Risks covered: expropriation and war & civil disturbance for up to 15 years.
